title: Breaking contact with a monster
target: How to get out of a monster's sight in R.E.P.O. — and what to do when running is not enough — using how it sees, how it takes damage and when it gives up.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A run with a monster awake
Something to hit with, or objects to throw
A level with somewhere to break line of sight

steps.do: Change your posture before you change your distance.
steps.because: how visible a player is has separate values for standing, crouching and crawling (VisionDotStanding, VisionDotCrouch, VisionDotCrawl)

steps.do: Know that how many sightings it takes differs by posture too.
steps.because: the number of sightings needed to trigger is separate for standing, crouching and crawling (VisionsToTrigger, VisionsToTriggerCrouch, VisionsToTriggerCrawl)

steps.do: Put distance between you and the point it sees from, not between you and the model.
steps.because: a monster has a vision point and a vision distance of its own, with a closer distance for a crouching player (VisionTransform, VisionDistance, VisionDistanceClose, VisionDistanceCloseCrouch)

steps.do: Do not treat objects as cover.
steps.because: objects are seen as well, with their own value and a radius that can be overridden (PhysObjectVision, PhysObjectVisionDot, PhysObjectVisionRadiusOverride)

steps.do: Hit it if you can, because it can be hurt rather than only avoided.
steps.because: a monster carries a health total and impacts hurt it with separate damage for a light, a medium and a heavy one (EnemyHealth, health, impactHurt, impactLightDamage, impactMediumDamage, impactHeavyDamage)

steps.do: Throw something when your weapon is out of the picture.
steps.because: being hurt by an object has its own switch, a multiplier and an option to stun (objectHurt, objectHurtMultiplier, objectHurtStun)

steps.do: Use a pit if the level has one.
steps.because: a monster checks whether it is over a pit, with transforms, a distance and a direction of its own (EnemyPitCheck, pitCheckTransforms, pitCheckDistance, isOverPit)

steps.do: Expect the chase to end by itself rather than lasting the whole run.
steps.because: a chase despawns after a time, and a monster that is stuck despawns with a count of its own (ChaseDespawn, DespawnAfterChaseTime, EnemyStateDespawn, StuckDespawn, StuckDespawnCount)

commonMistakes: Backing away while standing upright, which keeps you as visible as you were.
Hiding behind an object a monster can see just as easily as it sees you.
Running with an empty weapon instead of throwing what is in reach.
Assuming a monster that has stopped chasing has left the level.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
